guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the strongest case for Texas comes through the air. Our longer-run numbers show a substantial advantage for the Texas passing offense against UT San Antonio’s pass defense. The opener illustrated that ceiling: Arch Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns, while Ryan Wingo added 121 receiving yards and a score. We are not treating one performance as proof, but the combination of quarterback production and four returning offensive-line starters supports the underlying matchup advantage.

The question is whether that advantage produces enough separation. Our numbers give UT San Antonio’s passing offense a plausible path to move the ball against a Texas pass defense that has not graded as strongly as the rest of the team. Texas forced three turnovers in its opener and has created at least one takeaway in 24 consecutive home games, but turnover production does not erase the potential for UT San Antonio to sustain some drives. With our model and the market expressing essentially the same expectation, we do not see enough pricing room to take a side.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Texas’ passing game against the UT San Antonio secondary. Texas generated 516 total yards at 7.0 yards per play in the opener, and Manning’s connection with Wingo showed how quickly this offense can create explosive production. That matters because our matchup numbers identify this as Texas’ clearest advantage, but the betting question is not simply whether Texas moves the ball—it is whether that success translates into consistent margin throughout the game.

recent_game.fact: Texas opened the 2026 season with a 59-7 home win over Texas State on Sept. 5.
Texas produced 516 total yards and averaged 7.0 yards per play against Texas State.
Texas rushed for 156 yards and three touchdowns against Texas State.
Texas forced three turnovers—two fumbles and one interception—against Texas State.

opponent_notes.fact: Texas and UTSA are scheduled to meet for the third time, with all three games played in Austin.
Texas defeated UTSA 41-20 in 2022 and 56-7 in 2024.
Against UTSA in 2024, Arch Manning recorded a 75-yard touchdown pass to Ryan Wingo and a 67-yard touchdown run.
Manning accounted for five touchdowns against UTSA in 2024, including four passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown.
Texas rushed for 187 yards against UTSA in 2024.

quarterback.fact: Senior quarterback Arch Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns in the 2026 opener against Texas State.
Manning is 13-3 as a Texas starter and 9-0 as a starter at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium.
In 2025, Manning completed 248 of 404 passes for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns while adding 399 rushing yards and a team-high 10 rushing touchdowns.
Manning has thrown a touchdown pass in every home game in which he attempted at least 10 passes.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running backs Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers transferred to Texas in spring 2026 from Arizona State and NC State, respectively.
Smothers totaled 100 yards from scrimmage against Texas State, rushing seven times for 72 yards and catching three passes for 28 yards and a touchdown.
Brown recorded 11 carries for 34 yards and two touchdowns in his Texas debut against Texas State.
Ryan Wingo caught seven passes for 121 yards and one touchdown against Texas State.
Auburn transfer Cam Coleman caught three passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns in his Texas debut against Texas State.

Texas added 2026 defensive transfers Rasheem Biles, Markus Boswell, Justin Cryer, Darius Snow, Ian Geffrard, Zion Williams, Nick Hudson and Bo Mascoe.
